claims.paraphrase: Page title.
Page tagline.
Section heading.
Setup needs Node.js 24 or later on a Mac or Linux computer.
Setup needs an existing GitHub account and Cloudflare account; the tool creates neither.
Opening either account is free.
The tool checks the Node version itself before asking any question.
Windows is unsupported; a Windows run fails partway with an unclear error; use WSL instead.
A developer can set the site up and hand it over.
Section heading.
The setup command is npx create-cairn-site.
Terminal excerpts come from recorded fixtures of a real setup.
The tool opens with the cost picture, the same facts as the earlier page.
Transcript block quoting the start of the cost preamble.
Five questions: name, description, brand color, AI-crawler stance, folder.
Enter accepts defaults for name and folder, skips optional fields, and no preference is preselected.
The run scaffolds locally, then GitHub, then Cloudflare, each stage asking first.
Section heading.
Transition into the consent prompt.
Transcript block: GitHub App and repository confirmation prompt.
Yes creates a private repository and an App used only by this site.
The App lets the tool and writers publish without personal GitHub accounts.
GitHub cannot reduce App permissions later.
The workflow permission lets the tool push the scaffold check workflow.
Two browser trips: create the App, then install it and sign in to GitHub.
An organization owner may need to approve the install; the tool stops and resumes.
Section heading.
The tool asks whether to install, build, and deploy now.
Definition of deploy as putting the site live.
Yes installs dependencies, signs in to Cloudflare if needed, and deploys.
Deploying creates one Worker, two databases, and one storage bucket.
The Worker runs on Workers Paid at five dollars a month from deploy.
Databases, bucket, and repository cost nothing at this scale.
Content lives in the GitHub repository, not in either database.
The tool moves the App private key into a Worker secret.
It asks for the sign-in email, writes the owner record, and opens a sign-in page.
Clicking Sign in there lands you signed in as owner, the last browser step.
Diagram: scaffold, GitHub create and install, Cloudflare sign-in and deploy, then sign-in page.
Three browser moments, four when Cloudflare sign-in is needed.
Section heading.
Transcript block: closing summary with URLs and what exists now.
Landing on the admin already signed in means setup finished.
Pointer to what a second editor needs.
The workers.dev address keeps working after a domain is connected.
Section heading.
The sign-in link the tool opens works for ten minutes.
Run create-cairn-site with --dir and --sign-in for a fresh link.
The command writes a link into the database and opens it with no email.
It works at any point after the site is live, from the creating machine.
A session created through the link lasts 30 days.
Earlier failures go to setup recovery.
